To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

an L-amino acid oxidase from L. muta venom has crystallized in space group P2(1), with unit-cell parameters of a = 66.05,  b = 79.41,  c = 100.52 Å and β = 96.55°, and that the asymmetric unit contains two molecules.
we have determined the crystal structure of a Lachesis mutat venom L-amino-acids oxidase at 3.2 Å resolution and that the structure reveals the presence of a new domain in the protein.
we crystallized and determined the structure of an L-aminois acid oxidase from L. muta venom, which has potential for the design of new therapeutics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and structural basis of the toxicity of snake-venom proteins, which is of interest to the understanding of the pathogenesis of envenoming and the design of antivenoms.
the isolation, purification and characterization of the venom of the South American pit viper Lachesis mutin and the molecular characterization of the venom components.
the structural and functional analysis of snake-venom proteins and their role in the defence of snakes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the L. muta LAAO is a novel member of the LAAO family and that the structure determination of L. muta will contribute to the understanding of the structural modifications in LAAOs that result in toxicity.
the L-amino-acids oxidases from the snake venoms are the result of the recruitment of non-toxic proteins that have undergone structural modifications to become toxic.

L-amino-acids oxidase from L. muta venom has a high potential for the development of novel anticoagulants, anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor drugs, as well as for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallization of an L-aminois oxidase from L. muta venom has provided a platform to understand the molecular mechanisms that result in toxicity.
the crystal structure of Lachesis mutina venom L-amino acid oxidase has been solved and refined to 3 Å resolution.
the crystal structure of an L-aminois acid oxidase from L. muta has been determined at 3.1 Å resolution and that the enzyme belongs to the α/β class of enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L. muta LAAO has a novel fold that is distinct from the other LAAOs.
snake venom LAAOs are structurally similar to mammalian LAAOs and the structural differences are not responsible for their toxicities.
